review.summary:
Phase 23 (AIRS management compatibility and security qualification) delivers real, executed cumulative offline qualification at source 79f03235ed349d674019b834fc9304b110273738f6f213a784b6bcf983b3965e, and the corrections requested by the rejected attempt-01 phase review are genuinely present in current source rather than asserted.

Evidence is executed, not registered. docs/reviews/phase-23-attempt-02.checks.json records exactly 71 commands, every one exit_code 0 with timeout false and source_unchanged true (20:31:34 to 21:13:14 UTC), and the command vector equals tools/check_phase.py management_commands(23) (14 scripts/check-rust.py receipts, 2 check-native-exports, 2 check-management-package, terminal red_team_management.py --check --require-through-phase 23 --verify-package-receipts). docs/checks/phase-23.json carries the identical header with passed true and no failing record. The run was a resumed run completed inside the source-and-plan-bound eight-hour window (docs/checks/phase-23-partial.json: same source, complete true). The 1.89.0 red-team receipt proves execution rather than compilation: cargo fmt --check, check/clippy --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test --workspace with 169 unit tests, 13 red_team_management_contracts, 3 red_team_management_fixtures, 6 red_team_management_models, the 28 red-team vendor contracts, 10 response-default/oracle tests, doctests, and cargo run --example red_team_management, all ok on MSRV.

Attempt-01's only medium is genuinely closed. scripts/check-package.py:107 injects '[features] red-team = ["scm-sdk/red-team"]' into the synthesized consumer, the four consumer runs use 'run --features red-team' (docs/checks/phase-23-package-1.89.0.json:989-1053, no unexpected-cfg warnings), and scripts/check-management-package.py:96 requires features == {'red-team': ['scm-sdk/red-team']}, so the previously no-op cfg body cannot be selected. The empty stdout at the red_team_dataplane index is inherent: contracts/compatibility/management-old-consumers/0.2.2/red_team_dataplane.rs:38-49 contains no println and exercises the builder, Nullable::Null and build_validated. Seven of the eight attempt-01 lows are closed in source: phase and chunk scopes gained from_attempt 2 revisions covering generated.rs, schema_graph.json, the union ledger, model tests, the example and both NOTICE files (docs/phase-status.json:5858-5997); management_fixtures.py:99 adds expectationsOrigin; check_phase.py:845-846 and review_phase.py:220-221 re-verify checkpoint bindings before a passing report and at review time; check-management-package.py:46-49 resolves the local rustc host/version; check-package.py:44-47 makes the development/credential prefix guard reachable; red_team_management.py:632-636 and :772-775 bind and grep the three fixture test names; the overlay records unionDecodeTransitions (contracts/red-team-management-model-overlay.json:48-65) rendered into docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:36-37; the unused import is gone.

Runtime design is correct and minimal. tools/red_team_management_models.py:195-216 requires the six projection nodes, two union nodes and two enum nodes to equal the frozen baseline byte-for-byte, asserts the legacy union branch count before appending exactly one tail, and :141-193 fails closed on unreviewed fragment vocabulary, string formats, patterns outside the three reviewed Vertex regexes, any default other than the client_session const, unreviewed additionalProperties policies, and divergent masked counterparts. The enum split is real in generated code: s012061/s012067 are the request-embedded nodes (generated.rs:174689 TargetCreateRequestConnectionType with VERTEXAI/N8N, :174760 TargetCreateRequestResponseMode with REALTIME) while frozen-parity TargetConnectionType (:174153) and ResponseMode (:162443) keep only old variants plus Unknown(String); red_team_management_models.rs:119-164 asserts both levels. Projection codecs decode to Patch and losslessly re-insert the raw value on failure with typed-over-raw serialization and baseline-collision errors (generated.rs:9313-9392), exercised across 84 vendor-derived cases in three modes. All five target response declarations are wire-asserted for operation name, method, exact /mgmt-plane path, both response modes, masked and credential-bearing branches and secret-free Debug across 5 providers x 4 auth shapes (red_team_management_contracts.rs:345-459). profiling_status validates against the vendor-derived TARGET_PROFILING_FILTER_VALUES before token acquisition or dispatch (targets.rs:84-91; red_team_management.rs:359-361) and propagates with exact query-pair counts over list/pages/items/all, while legacy status=QUEUED rides unchanged with accurate rustdoc naming the five values upstream no longer declares (targets.rs:26-46).

Boundaries hold. contracts/qualification.json:34-42 reports liveReceipt null, liveVerified 0, liveNotVerified 448; red_team_management.py:749-763 rejects any current live receipt or leaked live annotation; live_evidence.py and check-access-release.py are excluded from phase 23 with recorded reasons; CI runs only the 51-command contracts subset alongside the 48-job matrix, with docs/CI.md's 71/51 counts bound to the derived lists by tools/test_ci.py:131-146. Old-consumer compatibility uses real published bytes pinned to the verified 0.2.2 registry archive and the phase-20 receipt (tools/management_consumers.py:38-85). CHANGELOG.md correctly carries no 0.2.3 entry; version selection, migration guidance, live tenant qualification and publication are phase 24.

Residual defects are all low and all cosmetic or evidence-hardening: the doc-before-attributes correction reached only one of three injected declarations, the delivered example's single filter assertion is tautological, archive-internal command cwd and a relative retainedArchive are unbound in receipt verification, 'no new preserve_order' is true in fact (Cargo.toml:44) but unenforced by any executed check, and the private-material receipt's headCommit is one commit behind HEAD with only format validation. No blocker or high finding. Total 46.5/50 with every category at or above 8 meets the phase gate.

findings.description: The attempt-01 required fix ("place generated documentation before attributes") was applied only to VertexAIConnectionRedactParams, where the anchor targets the full declaration block and the reviewed doc correctly precedes #[derive] (crates/scm-sdk/src/models/red_team_management.rs:240-246). The two frozen-parity enum doc injections still anchor on 'pub enum NAME {', so their reviewed doc comments are emitted after #[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq)] and #[non_exhaustive]: crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs:162439-162443 (ResponseMode) and :174149-174153 (TargetConnectionType). This compiles and renders in rustdoc, but it is the same inconsistency the earlier finding asked to remove, so the correction is only partially delivered across the phase.
findings.required_fix: Change the replace_once anchor at tools/generate_models.py:1063 to target the attribute block preceding each enum (for example the '#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\n#[non_exhaustive]\npub enum NAME {' span) so the injected doc comment precedes #[derive]/#[non_exhaustive], then regenerate and re-record tools/generate_models.py --check.

findings.description: The example's only assertion about the new profiling filter is assert_eq!(listing.profiling_status.as_deref(), Some("COMPLETED")), which merely re-reads the value assigned at :83 and demonstrates nothing about the feature. The example is bound as runtime evidence (contracts/red-team-management-model-overlay.json sourceBindings and the executed 'cargo run --example red_team_management' receipts on both compilers, plus the packaged external-consumer run at docs/checks/phase-23-package-1.89.0.json:1052), so a reader may mistake it for filter verification. The real coverage is in crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_management_contracts.rs:466-558 and is not referenced from the example.
findings.required_fix: Replace the tautological assertion with a meaningful offline demonstration (for example constructing TargetListOptions with an undeclared value and showing RedTeamTargetsClient::list_pages returns ErrorKind::Validation with no transport) or add a comment pointing at crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_management_contracts.rs:466-558 for the executable filter/pagination evidence.

findings.description: verify_receipt proves the four required archive-internal commands ('test --lib --no-default-features', 'test --lib --all-features', 'check --examples --all-features', 'test --doc --all-features') and the four 'run --example <name> --all-features' invocations are present only by matching the command vector. Unlike the consumer and frozen-probe bindings at :105 and :118, their 'cwd' is never bound, so a receipt whose archive-internal commands were executed in the repository checkout rather than the extracted archive would still verify. The actual runs are correct (docs/checks/phase-23-package-1.89.0.json records cwd /tmp/scm-sdk-archive-fuz85cow/scm-sdk), so this is an evidence-integrity hardening gap rather than a false claim.
findings.required_fix: Bind the cwd of every required and packaged-example check to the extracted archive root (for example require pathlib.Path(row['cwd']).name == 'scm-sdk' and that it differs from the repository root and the consumer directory), and add a tools/test_management_package.py case rejecting a receipt whose archive-internal command recorded a different working directory.

findings.description: archive = pathlib.Path(report['retainedArchive']) is used as given. A relative value would resolve against the verifying process's working directory instead of the repository root, unlike tools/check_phase.py:749-752 which anchors a relative retainedArchive to root before hashing it. Current receipts record absolute paths under .local/package-worktrees/06954db.../.local/artifacts/, so verification is sound today, but the check is weaker than its sibling and could bind a different file when invoked from another directory.
findings.required_fix: Anchor the value the same way as tools/check_phase.py:749-752 (resolve relative paths against root) and require an absolute, non-symlinked regular file; add a tools/test_management_package.py case covering a relative retainedArchive value.

findings.description: The phase 23 required evidence 'no new preserve_order' is not enforced by any command in commands_for(23). I verified the fact independently (crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml:44 declares serde_json features = ["raw_value"], and the only repository source occurrence of the token is the unrelated pagination test name page_and_item_iteration_preserve_order_and_duplicate_rows), but docs/checks/phase-23-dependencies.json records no resolved-feature ledger, so neither a direct nor a transitive enablement of serde_json/preserve_order would be caught by a check. The requirement currently rests on reviewer inspection.
findings.required_fix: Record and assert resolved features in scripts/check-dependencies.py from 'cargo metadata --all-features' resolve nodes (requiring serde_json's resolved feature set to exclude preserve_order), or add an explicit assertion in tools/test_dependency_policy.py or tools/test_management_phases.py that the serde_json manifest feature set equals {"raw_value"} and that no workspace feature forwards preserve_order.

findings.description: check_receipt re-binds the receipt's sourceSha256 and published-candidate fingerprints to current bytes, but validates headCommit only as a 40-64 character hex string. docs/checks/phase-23-private-material.json:5 records headCommit cd6600c53ba92afb8ded1dc8ea3221b7640c24a3 while the qualified release commit is 06954db447f3ff8023d86fe870865ed0f9418527 (recorded in both package receipts). Content coverage is sound because git_files includes untracked files and the source_only fingerprint matches 79f0323..., and the historical-versus-introduced tenant-occurrence classification against an older head is conservative, but the receipt does not bind repository history identity, so a scan performed at a different commit with identical source content still verifies for the current gate.
findings.required_fix: Require the receipt's headCommit to equal the current 'git rev-parse HEAD' in check_receipt (or record and compare it in tools/check_phase.py's phase-23 checkpoint bindings), and add a test rejecting a receipt whose headCommit differs from the verified source commit.

evidence: docs/reviews/phase-23-attempt-02.checks.json:1-6 records phase 23, source_sha256 79f03235ed349d674019b834fc9304b110273738f6f213a784b6bcf983b3965e, source_unchanged true, passed true, checked_at 2026-10-19T21:13:14.081169+00:00. A count over the file returns exactly 71 occurrences of "exit_code": 0 and zero matches for "exit_code": [1-9], "timeout": true or "source_unchanged": false. docs/checks/phase-23.json carries the identical header and the same 71 passing records with no failing match.

The recorded command plan equals tools/check_phase.py management_commands(23) (lines 189-285): extracting script paths from the checks file yields 14 scripts/check-rust.py invocations, 2 scripts/check-native-exports.py, 2 scripts/check-management-package.py, and a terminal tools/red_team_management.py --check --require-through-phase 23 --verify-package-receipts (checks.json:1864-1888, stdout 'AIRS contracts: 7 source pins, 160 operation mappings, 42 management operations; static evidence only'), with check-package.py and live_evidence.py correctly absent per the exclusions at check_phase.py:263-268.

Rust evidence is executed, not compiled: docs/checks/phase-23-rust-1.89.0-red-team.json:8-15 records rustc 1.89.0 host x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, and the 'cargo test --workspace --no-default-features --features red-team' record at :80-91 shows 169 unit tests ok (including airs::red_team::targets::tests::profiling_filter_rejects_undeclared_values and profiling_filter_preserves_legacy_status_without_translation), 13 red_team_management_contracts ok, 3 red_team_management_fixtures ok, 6 red_team_management_models ok, 28 red_team_contracts ok, 21 red_team_resources_contracts ok, 10 response-default/oracle tests ok, and doctests ok.

Both compilers ran the source-matched clean package wrapper and both receipts are source-bound: checks.json:1806-1862 records check-management-package.py for 1.89.0 (373.3s, 'HEAD is now at 06954db', archive 23a152c1...) and 1.99.0 (357.6s, archive 7de5e2db...), each with checkpoint_bindings covering the receipt and the retained archive bytes. docs/checks/phase-23-package-1.89.0.json:1061-1067 records sourceSha256 79f03235..., packageScriptSha256, wrapperSha256, oldConsumerManifestSha256 10cecd5e... and the four published consumer hashes; scripts/check-management-package.py:139-163 packages from a detached worktree whose fingerprint must equal the reviewed source before and after, then re-verifies the receipt.

The attempt-01 medium is genuinely closed: scripts/check-package.py:100-107 rejects an ambiguous manifest and injects '[features]\nred-team = ["scm-sdk/red-team"]', :213 runs each frozen consumer with 'run --features red-team', docs/checks/phase-23-package-1.89.0.json:989-1053 shows all four consumer runs at exit 0 with no 'unexpected cfg condition value' warnings, and scripts/check-management-package.py:94-97 requires tomllib.loads(manifest)['features'] == {'red-team': ['scm-sdk/red-team']}. The one empty stdout is inherent: contracts/compatibility/management-old-consumers/0.2.2/red_team_dataplane.rs:37-49 has no println and instead exercises ThreatOverrideItem::builder, Nullable::Null and build_validated.

Runtime graph change is provably minimal and fail-closed: tools/red_team_management_models.py:195-201 requires every projection, union and enum node to equal the frozen typescript.json baseline byte-for-byte before adoption; :212-215 asserts the legacy branch count (4 for s010462, 2 for s010504) before appending exactly one tail; :141-193 rejects unreviewed fragment vocabulary, string formats, any pattern outside the three reviewed Vertex regexes, any default other than the client_session const, unreviewed records/additionalProperties policies; :74-95 requires exact vendor projection component/field coverage and identical masked counterparts; :268-284 strips the reviewed tail before delegating to the strict baseline union verifier.

The enum split is correct in generated code: generated.rs:174689 declares TargetCreateRequestConnectionType for frozen schema s012061 with VERTEXAI and N8N added, :174760 declares TargetCreateRequestResponseMode for s012067 with REALTIME, while :174149-174166 (TargetConnectionType) and :162439-162449 (ResponseMode) keep only frozen variants plus Unknown(String). crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_management_models.rs:119-132 asserts validation::parse("s012061", "REALTIME", Request) fails while s012067 accepts it, and :134-164 asserts the named variants on the schema-bound enums and Unknown("VERTEX_AI")/Unknown("REALTIME") on the frozen constants.

Five response declarations are wire-asserted: crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_management_contracts.rs:345-459 drives get/create/update/probe/update_profile through an injected transport over 5 providers x 4 auth shapes x 2 response modes, asserting operation names, HTTP methods, exact paths under /mgmt-plane, byte-exact equality in ResponseWithoutDefaults, validator-normalized equality in Response, masked and credential-bearing branches, and absence of the synthetic secret in both Debug and the transport request. tools/red_team_management.py:648-686 derives those rows from the vendor spec, requiring required-field equality, full vendor-property coverage and nullable acceptance against the retained root.

Filter behaviour and pre-auth rejection: targets.rs:84-91 validates against TARGET_PROFILING_FILTER_VALUES (crates/scm-sdk/src/models/red_team_management.rs:359-361 = ["NOT_STARTED","IN_PROGRESS","COMPLETED","FAILED"], emitted from the vendor ProfilingStatusFilter enum at red_team_management_models.py:244-247) and returns ErrorKind::Validation before common::listing dispatch; list_pages:350 validates before constructing the walk and clones the params per page; contracts.rs:466-539 asserts exact query-pair counts on every page of list/pages/items/all for all four accepted values while legacy status=QUEUED rides unchanged, and :540-558 asserts zero token acquisitions and zero dispatches for five invalid values across all four surfaces.

Typed projection semantics verified in generated code: generated.rs:9313-9352 removes basic_username/basic_password, decodes to Patch and re-inserts the raw value into the baseline map on decode failure; :9354-9392 serializes typed values first, errors on baseline-key extension collisions and skips colliding extension keys. red_team_management_fixtures.rs:57-88 exercises all 84 vendor-derived cases in three modes against independently authored raw expectations with typedPresence and secret-free Debug assertions, and contracts.rs:572-602 proves typed override and unset restore for both field families.

Offline/live and CI boundaries hold: contracts/qualification.json:34-42 has liveReceipt null, liveVerified 0, liveRecorded 0, liveNotVerified 448; tools/red_team_management.py:749-763 rejects any current contracts/live-evidence.json, nonzero liveVerified or leaked liveEvidence row; tools/test_ci.py:131-146 binds docs/CI.md's 'complete local Phase 23 gate has 71 commands' and 'CI's 51-command subset' to len(commands_for(23)) and len(ci_commands_for(23)), and :528-530 requires the workflow to run --phase 23 --verification-only --contracts-only writing phase-23-contracts.json and never phase-23.json. README.md:88-92 and docs/CI.md:159-175 state the archived 0.2.2 receipt does not qualify the current management changes.

Old-consumer compatibility uses real published bytes: tools/management_consumers.py:14-17 pins the manifest sha256 10cecd5e..., the 0.2.2 registry archive c908cad8b27863d0e2d3987f5554b196313877788ac8cfef35c16d589910db7c and release commit 0716cfdc...; :62-84 requires each frozen file's bytes to equal the published archive member or the phase-20 receipt field, requires current repository bytes to equal the frozen bytes, rejects symlinks, path escapes and unowned/missing frozen files, and prints executionClaimed false. Those same four hashes appear as the executed consumers in both package receipts.

Supporting documentation and legal notices are current: NOTICE:10-15 and crates/scm-sdk/NOTICE name pan.dev revision 582e30543bf2adfd8b0ee457170d22b5c380dfbe, OpenAPI 0.86.0 alongside the data-plane revision under the MIT notice; docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:30-37 discloses the typed-relocation behaviour change and both Unknown(JsonValue)-to-named-variant transitions; targets.rs:26-46 names the five legacy status values upstream no longer declares with the unchanged-wire caveat; CHANGELOG.md:1-9 correctly carries no 0.2.3 entry, deferring release notes to phase 24.

Gate machinery is sound: tools/check_phase.py:780-784 recomputes every record's checkpoint bindings and :845-846 re-verifies them before writing a passing phase-23 report; tools/review_phase.py:201-222 requires the complete commands_for(phase) list, passed true, scope absent, matching source hash, and re-verifies bindings for phases 23-25 on current source; :69-86 implements the current rubric (chunk >=42, phase >=46, every category >=8, blocker/high always rejecting, attempt-five >40 requiring four completed prior reviews); :232-253 and :356-372 enforce versioned chunk scope revisions and restrict the chunk follow-up path. docs/checks/phase-23-partial.json records the same source with complete true inside the eight-hour window.
limitations: Read-only Read/Glob/Grep only; Bash was not used. I executed no command and recomputed no SHA256, so the declared reviewed-source hash 79f0323... and checks hash 955bd2a9... are taken as given. I verified internal consistency instead: per-record exit codes, timeout and source_unchanged flags, the derived command-plan equality, receipt sourceSha256/archive/consumer hashes, checkpoint-binding structure, and the source-binding logic in the verifying scripts.
No check was re-executed. Pass/fail conclusions rest on the recorded invocations, exit codes and stdout/stderr in the receipts plus the fail-closed logic in the tools.

docs/checks/* and docs/reviews/* are excluded from the review fingerprint (tools/review_phase.py:15-16) and several phase-23 receipts are modified or untracked, so their bytes lie outside the reviewed source hash; they are bound by the recorded checkpoint_bindings and by the final --verify-package-receipts gate.

The retained clean archives live at untracked absolute paths under .local/package-worktrees/06954db.../.local/artifacts/; I did not read those bytes, so archive_sha256 23a152c1... and 7de5e2db... are supported only by the receipts' member ledgers and the per-file source-equality checks in scripts/check-management-package.py:56-73.

Generated model correctness was assessed through the compiler receipts, selected generated declarations (the four enums, VertexAIConnectionParams/RedactParams, the BasicAuthAuthConfig projection codec) and the independent fixture/check evidence, not by reading the full 174k-line generated.rs or the minified schema_graph.json node by node.

The union acceptance expectations in contracts/native-fixtures/red-team-management.json remain reviewed, hand-authored vendor-schema-derived values rather than independent validator-oracle outputs. This is now explicitly disclosed (tools/management_fixtures.py:99 expectationsOrigin, asserted by tools/test_management_fixtures.py:20-21), but it is weaker evidence than the G25 Zod/AJV-oracle corpus. Raw preservation and default expectations are independent witnesses.

I did not re-derive the vendor OpenAPI content; pin verification (mp-openapi.yaml 5fbb533b..., openapi.json normalized equality) is taken from the tools' own guards, whose tamper tests are recorded as passing.
I read no credential or tenant-registration file and inspected nothing outside this repository.

Offline scope only. Nothing here establishes live service acceptance or remote CI coverage. Release version selection (the workspace is still 0.2.2), changelog migration guidance, controlled tenant qualification, publication, tagging and terminal remote CI are phase 24 deliverables and were not judged.

Both declared chunks are recorded as accepted at this same source hash (compatibility-matrix 46.5, package-security 46.0) at attempt 2, so the attempt-five chunk follow-up path in docs/PHASES.md:100-114 is not in play; docs/phase-status.json still lists both chunk statuses as 'pending' because the gate writes them only on phase acceptance, which I did not treat as a defect.

Cumulative inherited infrastructure (G25 corpora, gateway specimens, Portkey, data-plane ledgers, historical release receipts) was treated as passing input through its executed checks rather than re-audited, per the scoped-change instruction.
